chapters.title: Quicksort, random pivot, three-way partition

frames.caption: Quicksort, random pivot, three-way partition — O(n log n) expected time, O(log n) expected extra space. Input: sort_array(nums=[5, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0]). Step through to watch the code work on this input.
lt, i, gt = lo, lo, hi — lt = 0; i = 0; gt = 5 (< pivot | == pivot | unseen | > pivot)
nums[gt], nums[i] = nums[i], nums[gt]; gt -= 1 — swap nums[0] and nums[5]; gt = 4
nums[lt], nums[i] = nums[i], nums[lt]; lt += 1; i += 1 — swap nums[3] and nums[4]; lt = 4; i = 5
if lt - lo < hi - gt: → false (gt = 4, hi = 5, lo = 0, lt = 4) (recurse on the smaller side)
lt, i, gt = lo, lo, hi — lt = 0; i = 0; gt = 3 (< pivot | == pivot | unseen | > pivot)
nums[gt], nums[i] = nums[i], nums[gt]; gt -= 1 — swap nums[1] and nums[3]; gt = 2
if lt - lo < hi - gt: → true (gt = 1, hi = 3, lo = 0, lt = 0) (recurse on the smaller side)
lt, i, gt = lo, lo, hi — lt = 2; gt = 3 (< pivot | == pivot | unseen | > pivot)
if lt - lo < hi - gt: → false (gt = 3, hi = 3, lo = 2, lt = 2) (recurse on the smaller side)
